question: Can plausible unknown exterior geography improve the r38 fantasy-map fit without changing the planet or calibrated physics?
planet: Hold the current retrograde rotation and 33.5-degree tilt, Earth radius/gravity/day/year, orbit, radiation and all r38 physical parameters. These are the current-world assumptions, not a claim that the orbit/rotation equal modern Earth's.
screen: Mean-climate zonefit must exceed the same-resolution three-layout control by at least 0.002; overall strict agreement must not fall; no painted-zone recall may fall by more than 0.02; Mediterranean dry share must not increase and Cs share may fall at most 0.02. Record failures explicitly.
transfer: At most the highest-zonefit eligible scenario advances to paired downsample-8 control/candidate checks with the same three layouts. No publication from the coarse screen alone. Additional exterior layouts are required before any world-fit adoption.
accounting: Verify that mapped land/terrain/targets are unchanged and every member passes observed numerical checks. Only the declared off-map variables may change. Preserve shared physics and all target definitions.
limits: These are coherent local-exterior hypotheses within the existing procedural generator, not complete reconstructed continents. The global latitude land profile remains the model's Earth reference; no independent planetary GCM validation is implied.
